rows.reason: Fault fixed: five sentences; 'sat down on' (l.1) and 'led thence into a field' (l.2) verbatim; on the stile not in the field sets aside the within-span option, and 'into a field' rules out the lane pair.

Fault fixed: shows which way round: 'Lady Canterville's earnest request' and 'had consented to keep' are verbatim on l.14 (Mrs Otis named on l.13), so Lady Canterville asked and Mrs Otis agreed, ruling out the reversal; nowhere-else option set aside.

Last sentence 'Mrs Umney names Lady Eleanore later, on line 29, not Mrs Otis.' reads naturally as Mrs Umney naming Lady Eleanore rather than naming Mrs Otis; it needs to say it is Mrs Umney, not Mrs Otis, who names her. 'Her words before that are a polite way of speaking' leaves the words unquoted: quote 'I am afraid' (l.22). And 'she did not know what it really signified' (l.22) points the child at the content of option A ('Something she was quite unconscious of') without setting it aside as not what she takes the stain to be. Quotations are otherwise verbatim.

Fault fixed: 'the tipsy-cake' (l.16), 'No' and 'It's the pudden' (l.18), 'apricot roll-up' (l.19) verbatim; 'pudden' is linked to 'pudding'; Tom, not Maggie, names the roll-up, which sets aside the reversal.

Fault fixed: no 'turned round'; anchors on the stem's 'ran on deck' (l.2) right after 'should like an apple' (l.2); work over only sets the time (l.1); 'The watch' (l.2) is the one looking out for the island, which sets aside the cause-swap option.

Fault fixed: 'behind the peaceful and sunlit countryside' is the end of l.18 and 'rose ever' is now correctly on l.19, quoted as passage words rather than the script's own English; 'the long, gloomy curve of the moor' and 'old gabled houses' (l.17) verbatim.

Fault fixed: no 'stone'; 'pillars on either side, blotched with lichens' and 'surmounted by' (l.59), 'boars' heads of the Baskervilles' (l.60) verbatim; 'surmounted by' explained as topped by; tracery (l.58) assigned to the gates.

Fault fixed: anchors on 'herself literary' (start of l.8); 'on the strength' (l.6), 'manuscript sermons' and 'a pretty good library of divinity' (l.7) verbatim; the rector's-daughter option is set aside as not the reason given.
Fault fixed: 'only this morning' now correctly cited to l.21; 'read you a scene out of this month's number' (l.20) and 'the company' (l.21) verbatim; his line 18 remark set aside as not the request.
